title: Frontend's address pickers show five addresses at a time and make the trader submit a search to narrow them; Design release 1 lists every address and filters it as the trader types

finding.frontend: Each of the five party pickers shows five addresses at a time under numbered pagination — the captured place-of-origin picker reads "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over pages 1, 2, 3 and a Next link. Narrowing the list means typing into the Search box and pressing a separate secondary "Search" button, which posts the form and re-renders the page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-110, handled at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:95-104). Paging is a link, so there is no client-side script at all. A search that matches nothing replaces the whole table with one sentence, "No addresses match your search.", leaving the trader on a page with a Save and continue button and nothing to select. Page size is fixed at five (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10).
finding.prototype: Design release 1 lists every address for that party on one page and reports "Showing 9 out of 9 results" above the table. The search box is a `type="search"` input with a small magnifier button beside it, and typing filters the rows in the browser as the trader types — each row carries the text it is matched against and is hidden or shown on every keystroke, with the visible count updating in place (app/assets/javascripts/consignment-address-search.js:66-92). The captured filtered state shows "Romania" typed and the count reading "Showing 3 out of 9 results" with the page never reloaded. There is no pagination anywhere on the page and no submit involved in searching.
finding.difference: Replace the picker's server-side search and pagination with a full list the trader filters in the browser: render every address for that party, report "Showing N out of M results" above the table, and narrow the rows as the trader types rather than on a button press. The two halves are one change and should not be split — dropping the pagination without the live filter leaves a long list with a submit-to-search box, which is worse than either design. Two consequences to settle while doing it. First, the page size lives in the address-book service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10) and the service pages against the address-book API, so listing everything means asking that service for the whole book for an organisation rather than a page of it. Second, the picker must keep working without JavaScript; the existing Search button and paging links are the no-JS path and should stay as the fallback rather than being deleted. The empty result also stops being a dead sentence once the count is live, but the wording of "No addresses match your search." is part of the address-book route-out work raised separately.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding pagination or a submit-driven search on Design release 1's picker, or a live filter on the frontend's. The captured DOM of dr1-consignment-address-select carries no pagination element and its search button is `type="button"`; fe-address-picker-place-of-origin carries a `govuk-pagination` nav and a submit button named `action` with value `search`.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier both ways. grep for govuk-pagination in capture/html/prototype/dr1-consignment-address-select.html returns zero and its only search control is a type="button" with aria-label "Search" (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:87); fe-address-picker-place-of-origin.html carries the govuk-pagination nav and a submit button name="action" value="search". Checked the filter is live rather than assumed, per rubric 1: app/assets/javascripts/consignment-address-search.js:82 binds filterRows to the input event and updateVisibleCount rewrites the counter, and the captured filtered state proves it — dr1-consignment-address-select-search-filtered.html reads "Showing 3 out of 9 results" over three visible rows on a page that was never reloaded. Verified the frontend server round trip at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:101-104 (isSearchAction re-renders page 1) and the fixed page size at src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10. Read the picker macro whole at _address-picker.njk:64-111 and confirmed the no-match branch at :105-107 really does replace the table with one sentence while leaving Save and continue in place. Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-address-picker-place-of-origin.png (Search button, "Showing 5 of 13 addresses", pages 1 2 3 Next) and evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-consignment-address-select.png (magnifier button, "Select an address", "Showing 9 out of 9 results", nine rows, no pagination). CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands, and one line of the difference slot understates how ready the code is. It says listing everything means "asking that service for the whole book for an organisation rather than a page of it", which reads as work to be built; the call already exists and is already used. src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:101-121 exports `all`, which returns every saved address for an organisation, and the contact-address page calls it today (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:73 and :80). So the picker change is switching from `search` to `all` plus a client-side filter, not adding a new capability to the service — though `all` fetches page one and then every remaining page in parallel, so whoever does this should look at what that costs on a large book before pointing five pages at it. Two further things the prose leaves loose. The empty state is not symmetrical in the way the difference slot implies: Design release 1 has no empty-result message at all — filtering to nothing leaves "Showing 0 out of 9 results" above an empty table — so "No addresses match your search." has no counterpart to align to, and rewording it is part of the route-out work only in the sense that the route out is what the sentence is missing. Separately, and deliberately not raised: Design release 1's picker accepts a submit with nothing selected and silently redirects to /roles-and-addresses (app/routes.js:3855-3860), where Frontend shows "Select a consignor from the list" and keeps the trader on the page. That is prototype plumbing rather than a stated requirement — the view carries error markup at app/views/consignment-address-select.html:104-108 that nothing ever populates — so it is not a finding, and nobody should read this one as asking Frontend to drop that validation. Three more differences on this page pair that I checked and am deliberately not raising, so that a later reader knows they were looked at rather than missed. First, the picker's "View details" does different things on the two sides: Frontend opens a govuk-details disclosure in the row holding the full address, the phone number and the email, while Design release 1 links out to /address-book/<id>?return=<page> — the saved-address record page, which shows the same eight facts plus Edit and Delete buttons (dr1-address-book-view). No information is lost either way, and where that link should go is the address-book scope question, so it belongs to address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent and not here. Second, Frontend prints "Selected address: <name>" in an inset above the results when a selection is carried across a page (fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-selected); Design release 1 only re-checks the radio (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:136). That is something Frontend has and the design does not, so under the contract it is an observation and not a defect. Third, Frontend renders the address as one comma-joined line and Design release 1 as one line per address line; both then give country its own column, so the same facts are on the page either way.
